M16 - TEMPORARY PFU ESTIMATE + PRODUCTION READINESS. EVIDENCE FIRST: searched for any PFU figure GommaRush already holds. There is none - production document_charges is empty, no order_items.environmental_fee is populated, none of the 57 imported documents mentions PFU, and neither supplier feed carries a PFU column. The estimate amounts are therefore OWNER PLACEHOLDERS chosen for flow testing, not sourced tariffs, and they say so in their own version id ('gr-pfu-estimate-2026-09-placeholder-v1'). METHOD: banded by supplier-reported weight, which is the physical basis the real scheme uses and is present for 11,407 of 13,226 active products. Bands measured against the real catalogue: <=11kg EUR 3.00, 11-20kg EUR 6.00, 20-40kg EUR 12.00, >40kg EUR 25.00. Product-class fallback where weight is missing (1,819 products), then a conservative EUR 6.00 catch-all - the 11-20kg amount rather than the lowest, because an under-estimate is the failure nobody notices. Amounts are deliberately round so they cannot be mistaken for a published tariff. Deterministic, no I/O, no model call at transaction time. SAFETY: a new PfuStatus value ESTIMATED, separate from RULE_CALCULATED, which is resolved (carries an amount) but NOT verified (isVerifiedPfuStatus returns false). resolvePfu prefers supplier-stated, then a verified tariff, then the estimate - so populating VERIFIED_PFU_TARIFFS retires the estimate with NO code change. allowEstimate:false gives accounting-grade callers the old TO_CONFIRM refusal. estimatedPfu() is the only constructor and requires the estimate object, so an estimated amount cannot exist without its version. SNAPSHOT: pfu_status, pfu_estimate_version, vat_rate_percent and delivery_promise_max_days are first-class COLUMNS on sales_orders and sales_order_items, not jsonb, so 'which orders rest on an estimate?' is a WHERE clause. Two check constraints make it impossible to store ESTIMATED without a version, or a version without ESTIMATED. Historical totals are never rewritten. M10: production feed activation. Architecture chosen: the worker runs ON the FTP VM and calls a protected application endpoint over HTTPS (option B), rejecting direct Supabase writes (option A) because that would put the RLS-bypassing service-role key on a box exposed on port 21. The worker is a dependency-free bash script - no Node, no npm tree on that VM - that reads the spool directory LOCALLY, so no FTP client and no FTP credentials are involved in ingestion at all. It checks file stability (vsftpd STOR is not atomic), claims by atomic mv, checksums, gzips and uploads, drives the batched commit to completion, and archives ONLY then. Server side: bearer-token auth with constant-time compare, checksum re-verified against the received bytes, category detected from the wcat column (never the filename - truck's name is a strict prefix of PCR's), then analyzeCatalogueImport/commitCatalogueImport - the SAME path the admin upload screen uses, so there is one catalogue pipeline. importMode is hard-wired to 'partial' while D14 is open. The importer now dispatches its reader on the bytes (zip magic = workbook, else delimited text) so real CSV and the XLSX samples reach the same M8 commercial mapping. Admin feed-status block on /admin/catalogue reports last success AND last attempt per feed, freshness, filename, short checksum and row counts. +50 tests, including the bash worker executed against a stub server.

M10: vsftpd STOR is NOT atomic - the supplier's file appears at its final name and grows. The worker requires STABLE_SECONDS (default 90) of no modification, re-checks the size after claiming and returns the file if it moved, and the server re-hashes the received bytes against the declared checksum. A truncated upload hashes perfectly well and looks complete, so this is three independent guards on purpose.

M10: importMode is hard-wired to 'partial' in submitIntersprintFeed and is NOT a caller parameter. A 'complete' run is the only thing that may propose deactivating listings absent from a file, and D14 is unresolved. Do not make this configurable until a supplier statement settles snapshot semantics.

M10: the feed worker token is a SEPARATE, single-purpose credential. The Supabase service-role key must never reach the FTP VM: it bypasses RLS on customers, orders and logistics, and that box is exposed on port 21.

M10: production writes the EU-label header as 'Fuel efficiency' where the August samples wrote 'Fuel effeciency'. Neither is mapped - the catalogue has no EU-label columns beyond eprel_id - so the difference is recorded, not depended on.

M9: transport inclusion is a property of the RELEASE, not of a catalogue row. An observation built without a release quantity resolves to commercialMode 'unknown' and fails closed. M9: a commit applying zero rows is treated as a FAILURE and the file goes to failed/. An Inter-Sprint delivery always carries rows, so zero means the wrong file was read or something broke; filing it under processed would hide that and suppress the retry.

M9: the completion record is written BEFORE the file is moved. A crash between the two leaves a correct database and a misplaced file rather than the reverse - a file in the wrong directory is a tidying problem, a file marked processed that never was is a double-charge.
